The results obtained by calculations and measurements are compared. These comparisons confirm that notch analysis is effective as a means of evaluation of propagation paths.

articleTitle: Analysis of channel capacity of M-ary DPSK and D/sup 2/PSK with time-selective Rician fading
abstract: Channel capacities of M-ary differential phase shift keying (DPSK) and M-ary adjacent D/sup 2/PSK on the time-selective Rician fading channels are analyzed, using the probability distribution factors (PDF's) of the first-order and second-order phase errors in the output of the detectors. The analyses are carried out for the systems with hard decision and soft decision. It is found that in terms of channel capacities for both DPSK and D/sup 2/PSK with soft decision and M/spl rArr//spl infin/, the penalty for the slow Rayleigh fading channel compared with the AWGN channel is about 4.8 dB for a high SNR.

articleTitle: Some properties of multiple carriers and intermodulation
abstract: The statistics of the amplitude of a sum of sinusoids with more-or-less equal spacing in frequency are examined, with emphasis on the short quasi-periodic peaks characteristic of such sums. Various choices of reference phase for the sinusoids are considered, along with their effect on the amplitude peaks. By assuming a small cubic nonlinearity for an amplifier being fed by the sum of sinusoids, the output intermodulation peaking is related to the quasi-periodic peaking of the input amplitude. To explore a possible mechanism for slow variations in the relative reference phases of the sinusoids, the effect of passing flicker noise through the closed loop filter response of a phase-locked loop is considered.

articleTitle: Narrow-band small area microcellular mobile radio channel characterization using ray tracing technique
abstract: The simulation of a microcellular mobile radio propagation environment is performed using a modified ray tracing technique. The modified ray tracing also accounts for building edge diffraction using Keller's geometrical theory of diffraction. Narrowband small area statistics are investigated by fitting Nakagami, Rice and Rayleigh distributions. The physical significance of Nakagami 'm' parameter is presented. It may be used for system design.

articleTitle: Multi-carrier coded 16QAM system in land mobile radio communications
abstract: A multicarrier coded 16 quadrature amplitude modulation (16QAM) system is proposed to achieve high-quality and high bit rate transmission with high spectral efficiency in land mobile radio communications. The system employs a multicarrier transmission scheme to provide immunity against multipath fading distortion. The proposed system also employs pilot symbol aided 16QAM to increase spectral efficiency and a combination of forward error correction (FEC) and space diversity to improve the bit error ratio (BER) performance. Computer simulation shows that a BER of less than 10/sup -4/ is obtained over channels with severe frequency-selective fading with RMS delay spreads /spl les/7.3 /spl mu/sec. It is shown that the proposed system can achieve high-quality transmission with high spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Construction of optimal frequency hopping sequences for minimizing bit errors in selective fading channels characteristic to digital cellular systems
abstract: The problem of constructing frequency hopping patterns for use in time division multiple access-frequency division multiple access (TDMA-FDMA) cellular systems that employ frequency diversity to minimize bursty errors occurring due to the fading channel is discussed. Conditions under which two frequency and time channels fade independently in a mobile fading channel are reviewed. The construction of a family of effective frequency hop sequences for achieving maximum diversity is given. The construction is based on the theory of linear congruences, and the number of sequences for every integer is established. It is shown that when sequences are constructed using prime numbers they are also orthogonal. Examples of constructed sequences applicable to the Groupe Speciale Mobile (GSM) cellular system are given.

articleTitle: Diversity combined decision feedback equalizer of digital 16QAM for microcellular mobile radio communication systems
abstract: The contents of a fading equalization technique suitable for microcellular mobile radio communication systems to which 16 QAM (quadrature amplitude modulation) has been applied is described. A proposal is made for a new algorithm that is the adaptive algorithm of the DFE (decision feedback equalizer) used in the fading equalization technique. The results of computer simulation adopting the proposed system are shown.

articleTitle: A time diversity CDMA scheme employing orthogonal modulation for time varying channels
abstract: In order to increase the channel capacity of CDMA (code division multiple access) mobile and personal communication systems, a new time diversity CDMA scheme that employs orthogonal modulation is proposed. The time diversity CDMA scheme with orthogonal modulation reduces the required Eb/(No+Io) by 5 dB at Pe = 10/sup -2/ in Rayleigh fading environments with fDT (the product of Doppler frequency and one symbol duration) values ranging from 0.002 to 0.02. This improvement in required Eb/(No+Io) significantly increases the channel capacity of CDMA communication systems that have time varying channels. Computer simulation results show that the required time delay values of the time diversity scheme are resonably short (20-100 symbols for 10 kbps transmission) for fDT values ranging from 0.002 to 0.02.

articleTitle: Frame timing acquisition for direct sequence spread spectrum signals in time division duplex transmission
abstract: The frame timing acquisition, which is important for the time division duplex (TDD) mode of transmission in direct sequence spread spectrum (DS-SS) communications, is studied. In the TDD-DS-SS system, the frame timing and base station signal must be obtained in the presence of interference from other mobile users. It is shown that acquisition of noncontinuous TDD signals is possible after transmission of a few acquisition bursts. Computer simulation techniques are used to evaluate the performance of this method.

articleTitle: Statistical characterization of intermodulation products in a multicarrier LPA design
abstract: An approximation is developed by rigorous analysis and simulation for the probability density function of the amplitude of multicarrier intermodulation (IM) at any frequency of interest in an RF linear amplifier. The derived characterizing statistic of the distribution is a function of the carrier frequencies. The analysis shows that the IM product level generated by a nonlinear amplifier can be accurately modeled by a bivariate Gaussian distribution function. Thus, the amplitude of the IM products can in turn be statistically characterized by a Rayleigh distribution. Therefore, cochannel interfering IM products in a communication system can be modeled simply, by knowing the transmitted carrier frequencies, the associated average transmitted carrier signal power, and the desired received carrier frequency.

articleTitle: Air interface of the future European fully digital trunk radio system
abstract: The European Telecommunications Standard Institute (ETSI) plans to release the standard for a system known as TETRA (Trans-European Trunk Radio). The design of the radio interface is reported. After a brief explanation of the adopted time division multiple access (TDMA) frame structure and mapping of traffic and control channels, a detailed discussion is presented on: power control of the mobiles during the access to network; the achievable bit error rate (BER) on various propagation channels (including hilly and urban area); and an original scheme to improve the immunity against the cochannel interference.

articleTitle: A novel algorithm for the analysis of partial response binary CPM with h = 1/2
abstract: Partial response binary continuous phase modulation schemes with h = 1/2 can be characterized by a finite number of real-valued impulses C/sub N/(/spl tau/) and D/sub N/(/spl tau/), respectively, in both the lowpass and the bandpass domain at suitably chosen intermediate frequency. An algorithm for the determining of these impulses is presented. The algorithm can be applied in both simulations and experiments, and is therefore suitable for the functional test of modulator ICs.

articleTitle: Optimized channel access for dedicated road traffic radio networks
abstract: Future road traffic will increasingly rely on communication between vehicles or vehicles and an infrastructure. One main problem in these decentrally organized mobile radio LANs is to develop a suitable channel access protocol. The behavior of synchronous channel access protocols is investigated and compared with pure contention protocols, which are optimized for the demands of road traffic networks by varying packet length and reaccess delay. The protocol performance is evaluated in terms of throughput and delay, as well as the efficiency of the packeting scheme.

articleTitle: Histogram and integral based evaluation of an experimental inter vehicle communication trial
abstract: A new approach to evaluate experimental communications system tests is presented. Initial inter-vehicle communications test trials were performed. The equipment and the test scenarios are presented. The common approach of a histogram-based performance evaluation which considers the message loss ratio and the link interrupt ratio is compared to a new integral-based estimation method. Several test driving scenarios, including overtaking and oncoming traffic, are carried out, and the results are presented in histogram form and in integral-based form.

articleTitle: A design of digital syllabic compander using the mean absolute estimator
abstract: A simplified digital syllabic compander (SDSC) that can be used for noise compression over a poor radio channel is discussed. The SDSC proposed employs the mean absolute estimator and the damping factor for computing the scale parameters. From the simulations performed, the SDSC satisfies CCITT (International Telegraphy and Telephony Consultative Committee) G.162 specifications on nonlinear distortions and the transient response.

articleTitle: Fractional-bit detection with advanced sampling to combat multipath-induced error floor
abstract: In digital mobile communications, the error floor caused by time dispersion of the channel limits data rate even in low delay spread situations. The errors originate in the transition regions between adjacent symbols when deep fades occur. A detection method to reduce these errors, i.e., fractional bit differential detection with sample timing which is advanced from the average mean excess delay, avoiding the transition regions, is analyzed. Assuming a minimum shift keying (MSK) modulation format, the error probability is calculated and verified by a Monte Carlo software simulation. The approach increases the tolerable delay spread in an unequalized receiver, depending on the details of the delay power profile. These are accounted for by introducing an effective delay spread. Limiting the bandwidth tends to smear the transition regions over the entire bit duration, thus offsetting part of the method's benefit.

articleTitle: A spread spectrum communication system without reference signal for frequency-selective fading channel
abstract: The RAKE receiver for spread spectrum communication is a countermeasure against frequency-selective fading. In order to operate the RAKE receiver, the impulse response of the fading channel must be sounded. For this purpose, some reference signal is transmitted together with the information signal in conventional systems. A method in which no reference signal is required is proposed. In this method, different codes are assigned corresponding to input binary data. Techniques are proposed which reduce the harmful effects of residual autocorrelation and cross-correlation of the spectrum-spreading code. In this method, a threshold value is used, and the residual response of autocorrelation and cross-correlation is subtracted from the matched filter output signal determining the channel impulse response. Computer simulation results under a two-path fading model are shown. Bit error rate performance of the RAKE receiver is improved with the proposed channel estimation method.

articleTitle: A simplified approach to growth planning for cellular systems
abstract: Practical approaches are provided to projecting traffic growth for a new cellular system, determining growth statistics for existing systems, presenting criteria for transitioning from omnidirectional to sectored cells, providing guidelines for cell splitting, and proposing methods for the overall analysis of system traffic performance. The results provide the engineer with some simplified methods that can improve overall system performance.

articleTitle: Adaptive receiver consisting of Viterbi equalizer and sector-antenna diversity for cellular radio
abstract: By changing the total combined directivity of M-sectored antennas adaptively, the receiver accepts multipath signals which can be equalized by a 16-state Viterbi equalizer. The receiver rejects both multipath signals with longer delay time and cochannel interference by distinguishing them from desirable signals. Based on computer simulation results, the performance of the proposed receiver is analyzed, assuming a typical propagation model with Rayleigh-distributed multipath signals and cochannel interference.

articleTitle: Adopting the isomorphic emphasis to speech security on the time domain scrambling
abstract: The authors report that isomorphic emphasis succeeds in preventing speech quality degradation during time domain scrambling without any expansion of frequency occupancy bandwidth over radio security speech channels. The isomorphic emphasis is realized with the canonical form, which consists of a cascaded differentiator, time domain scrambler with arbitrary sequential pattern, and integrator. This time domain scrambler degrades speech quality by changing the power ratio of speech signal to fading noise over subjective frequency domain. The isomorphic emphasis is shown to protect time scrambled signals from both expansion and degradation over all of the subjective frequency domain, even if there exists a discontinuity among input data according to time scrambling. These facilities of the isomorphic emphasis in the time domain scrambling for speech security are verified from theoretical analysis and computer simulations for poor fading channels.

articleTitle: A direct conversion receiver for GMSK in digital mobile communications
abstract: Quadrature detection is applied to the direct conversion receiver for a Gaussian minimum shift keying (GMSK) signal which is implemented by one DSP chip, TMS320C25, and some supporting components at the bit rate of 72 kb/s. The frequency error estimation, timing recovery, and decision are all completed by software, which makes the receiver simple and flexible. Computer simulation results and test performance of the actual system are satisfactory. The system is easy to modify for different requirements and is suitable for discrete realization and integration.

articleTitle: Design of the Westinghouse Series 1000 mobile phone
abstract: The North American MSAT system will bring mobile satellite services to the communications industry. The system is described as it relates to the mobile unit. The Westinghouse unit, the Series 1000 Mobile Phone, is designed to render optimum performance at a low per unit cost.
